title: grant-armed/1
description: The record `bin/grant.py --arm` writes inside the repository's git directory, beside the armed goal's: what the person's own words let a session do at a stop, for one live initiative. «A grant is armed only by the person's own invocation of `/siegard-grant`, a skill closed to the model, whose arguments are the person's words.» (SPEC-011 R1)

project_root.description: The project the grant names, as the invocation spelled it.

slug.description: The one live initiative the grant covers, where the person names one; null where it covers every live initiative of the project.

target.description: The target whose records name the paths a commit may carry.

doors.description: The entry points a stop may take. «`analyse` is in `doors` only where the person writes it: no other entry point is, whatever the person writes.» (SPEC-011 R2)

budget.description: How many judged doors the grant lets the door decider choose, counted from the initiative's orchestration log.

commits.description: Whether a session may commit what the route wrote.

close.description: Whether a session may close an initiative where the state computation reads every task delivered, proven and reviewed; the person's words are the reason.

path.description: The file the words were copied to, whole and unedited, by `bin/ask.py --record`.

sha256.description: The first 16 hex characters of the words' sha256, the form an ask is named by.

version.description: The plugin's version at arming: the rules a grant took are those of its version.

since.description: Where `HEAD` stood at arming, from which the judged doors taken are counted.

allOf.$comment: A grant holds at least one clause.
